notes.definition: The velocity of an object is its speed in a given direction. Velocity is a vector quantity: it has both magnitude (the speed) and direction, and is measured in m/s.
explanation: Speed tells you how fast something is moving. Velocity tells you how fast it is moving and in which direction. For example, "15 m/s" is a speed, but "15 m/s north" is a velocity. Because velocity has both magnitude and direction it is a vector quantity, whereas speed is a scalar. Both are measured in metres per second (m/s).

The scalar and vector pairs fit together: distance (scalar) and displacement (vector), speed (scalar) and velocity (vector). Speed is distance travelled per second; velocity is displacement per second. For motion along a straight line, it helps to choose one direction as positive. Then a velocity of +4 m/s means 4 m/s in the positive direction and −4 m/s means 4 m/s in the opposite direction. The speed is 4 m/s in both cases.

Two objects can have the same speed but different velocities. Two cars travelling at 20 m/s on opposite sides of a motorway have the same speed, but one has a velocity of 20 m/s north and the other 20 m/s south. Velocity can therefore change in two ways: the speed can change, the direction can change, or both can change together.

Because velocity depends on displacement, average speed and average velocity can be very different. A runner who completes one 400 m lap in 80 s has an average speed of 400 ÷ 80 = 5 m/s. But she ends where she started, so her displacement is zero and her average velocity is zero. For a journey in one direction along a straight line, the average speed and the size of the average velocity are the same.

(Higher) An object moving in a circle at a constant speed has a changing velocity. At every point its velocity is directed along the tangent to the circle, and as it goes round the direction is continuously changing. Examples include a satellite orbiting the Earth, a car driving round a roundabout at a steady speed, the tip of a clock hand, or a ball whirled on a string. Since the velocity changes, the object is accelerating, even though its speed stays the same.
keyFacts: Velocity is speed in a given direction.
Velocity is a vector quantity; speed is a scalar quantity.
Velocity is measured in metres per second (m/s), the same unit as speed.
A velocity must always be stated with a direction, for example 12 m/s east, or a sign once a positive direction is chosen.
Two objects with the same speed have different velocities if they move in different directions.
Velocity changes if the speed changes, the direction changes, or both.
Average velocity uses displacement; average speed uses distance.
An object that returns to its starting point has an average velocity of zero.
(Higher) Motion in a circle at constant speed involves a continuously changing velocity.

keyTerms.definition: The speed of an object in a given direction. A vector quantity measured in m/s.
The distance travelled per unit time, with no direction. A scalar quantity measured in m/s.
A quantity with both magnitude and direction, for example velocity, displacement, force.
A quantity with magnitude only, for example speed, distance, time.
The size of a vector, ignoring direction. The magnitude of a velocity is the speed.
Velocity that does not change: constant speed in a straight line in one direction.

equations.name: Distance travelled at constant speed (used with displacement for velocity)
equations.units: s in metres (m), v in metres per second (m/s), t in seconds (s)

workedExamples.title: Calculating a velocity
workedExamples.question: A cyclist travels 450 m due south along a straight road in 75 s. Calculate her velocity.
steps: v = s ÷ t, using the displacement.
Give the direction: the velocity is 6.0 m/s south.

workedExamples.title: Average speed and average velocity
workedExamples.question: A man walks 90 m east in 60 s, then turns and walks 30 m west in 20 s. Calculate (a) his average speed and (b) his average velocity.
steps: Total distance = 90 + 30 = 120 m; total time = 60 + 20 = 80 s.
Displacement (east positive) = +90 − 30 = +60 m, so 60 m east.

workedExamples.title: Converting km/h and rearranging
workedExamples.question: An aircraft flies due west at a constant velocity of 900 km/h. Calculate its displacement after 4.0 minutes in metres.
steps: Convert the velocity to m/s: 900 × 1000 ÷ 3600 = 250 m/s.
Convert the time to seconds: 4.0 × 60 = 240 s.
Include the direction: 60 000 m (60 km) west.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think speed and velocity mean exactly the same thing.
misconceptions.right: In fact velocity is speed in a given direction. Speed is a scalar; velocity is a vector, so a velocity must include a direction.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think that if an object's speed is constant, its velocity must be constant too.
misconceptions.right: In fact velocity also changes if the direction changes. An object going round a circle at constant speed has a changing velocity.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think a negative velocity means the object is slowing down.
misconceptions.right: In fact a negative velocity only means the object is moving in the direction chosen as negative. It could be speeding up in that direction.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think average velocity is always the same as average speed.
misconceptions.right: In fact average velocity uses displacement, so if an object changes direction or returns to its start, the average velocity is smaller than the average speed (or zero).

realWorld: Air traffic controllers need each aircraft's velocity (speed and heading), not just its speed, to keep planes safely apart.
Weather forecasts give wind velocity as a speed and a direction, for example 8 m/s from the south west.
Satellites in circular orbits move at a steady speed but their velocity is constantly changing direction as they go round the Earth.
In football analysis, a ball's velocity (speed and direction) determines where a pass or shot will go.
higherTier: Explain qualitatively, with examples, that motion in a circle involves constant speed but changing velocity: the direction of motion (along the tangent) changes continuously, so the velocity changes even though the speed does not.
examTips: When a question asks for a velocity, always include a direction (north, left, up, or a sign) as well as the number and unit m/s.
In explain-the-difference questions, say: speed is a scalar (magnitude only); velocity is a vector (magnitude and direction); velocity is speed in a given direction.
For circular motion questions (Higher), state that the speed is constant but the direction changes, so the velocity changes. Saying only "it is moving in a circle" will not score.
Use displacement for velocity calculations and distance for speed calculations, and watch for journeys that return to the start.
summary: Velocity is speed in a given direction.
Velocity is a vector; speed is a scalar; both are in m/s.
Same speed in different directions means different velocities.
Velocity changes when speed or direction (or both) change.
Average velocity = displacement ÷ time; it can be zero when average speed is not.
(Higher) Circular motion at constant speed has a changing velocity.

flashcards.front: Is velocity a scalar or a vector?
flashcards.back: A vector: it has magnitude and direction.

flashcards.front: Which vector quantity pairs with distance?
Which vector quantity pairs with speed?
Two ways a velocity can change
flashcards.back: The speed changes or the direction changes (or both).

flashcards.front: Car X: 15 m/s north. Car Y: 15 m/s south. Same speed?
Car X: 15 m/s north. Car Y: 15 m/s south. Same velocity?
flashcards.back: No, they move in different directions.

flashcards.front: (Higher) Why does an object moving in a circle at constant speed have a changing velocity?
flashcards.back: Its direction of motion is continuously changing.

flashcards.front: Average velocity of a runner after one complete lap
flashcards.back: Zero, because the displacement is zero.

flashcards.front: What does a negative velocity mean?
flashcards.back: Moving in the direction chosen as negative (opposite to the positive direction).

flashcards.front: Give an example of motion at constant speed but changing velocity.
flashcards.back: A satellite in a circular orbit, a car on a roundabout at steady speed, the tip of a clock hand.

questions.question: Which statement best defines velocity?
options: The rate of change of speed
questions.explanation: Velocity is speed in a given direction. A is speed; C describes acceleration; D describes displacement.

questions.question: Which of these is a velocity?
questions.explanation: A velocity needs a speed unit and a direction. 30 m/s has no direction; 30 m north is a displacement; m/s² is the unit of acceleration.

questions.question: Which pair shows a scalar quantity followed by its matching vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Speed (scalar) pairs with velocity (vector). B and C have them the wrong way round; D gives two vectors.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows two trains, A and B, passing each other on parallel tracks.
Which statement is correct?
options: They have the same velocity and the same speed
They have different speeds but the same velocity
They have the same speed but different velocities
They have different speeds and different velocities
questions.explanation: Both have a speed of 40 m/s, but because they move in opposite directions their velocities are different (+40 m/s and −40 m/s).

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows a trolley on a track. Right is taken as the positive direction.
The trolley has a velocity of −2.5 m/s.
What does this tell you about the trolley?
options: The trolley is moving at 2.5 m/s to the left
The trolley is moving at 2.5 m/s to the right
questions.explanation: The negative sign shows direction only: the trolley is moving to the left at a speed of 2.5 m/s. It does not mean it is slowing down.

questions.question: Which of these changes would NOT change the velocity of a car?
options: Speeding up on a straight road
Turning a corner at a steady speed
Driving at a steady speed in a straight line
questions.explanation: Velocity only stays constant if both speed and direction stay the same. A and C change speed; B changes direction.

questions.question:
A swimmer swims 2 lengths of a 50 m pool in 80 s. She finishes where she started.
What is the average velocity of the swimmer?
questions.explanation: Her displacement is zero because she returns to her start, so her average velocity is zero. Her average speed is 100 ÷ 80 = 1.25 m/s.

questions.question:
A satellite orbits the Earth in a circle at a constant speed.
Which statement is correct?
options: Its velocity is constant because its speed is constant
It is not accelerating because its speed does not change
Its velocity is changing because its direction is changing
Its velocity is zero because it returns to the same point
questions.explanation: In circular motion the direction of motion changes continuously, so the velocity changes even though the speed is constant. A changing velocity means the satellite is accelerating.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows a car driving round a roundabout at a steady speed of 8 m/s, seen from above.
The car enters the roundabout heading north and leaves heading east.
Which describes the change in the motion of the car?
questions.explanation: The speed stays at 8 m/s, but the direction changed from north to east, so the velocity changed.

questions.question:
A runner moves 200 m due east along a straight path in 40 s.
Calculate the size of the velocity of the runner.
questions.explanation: v = s ÷ t = 200 ÷ 40 = 5.0 m/s. As a velocity, this is 5.0 m/s east.

questions.question:
A car travels north at a constant velocity of 25 m/s for 2.0 minutes.
Calculate the displacement of the car in metres.
questions.explanation: Convert minutes to seconds, then s = v t = 25 × 120 = 3000 m north.

questions.question:
A lorry travels south at 72 km/h.
Calculate the size of the velocity of the lorry in m/s.
questions.explanation: 72 km/h = 72 000 m ÷ 3600 s = 20 m/s, so the velocity is 20 m/s south.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows a boat and a buoy.
The boat sails due west at a constant velocity of 4.0 m/s.
Calculate the time taken for the boat to reach the buoy.

questions.question:
A dog runs in a straight line.
Table 1 shows information about the run.
Calculate the size of the average velocity of the dog for the whole run.
questions.explanation: Average velocity uses displacement: 30 m north in 24 s gives 1.25 m/s north. Using the distance (120 m) gives the average speed, 5.0 m/s.

questions.question:
A dog runs in a straight line.
Table 1 shows information about the run.
Calculate the average speed of the dog for the whole run.
questions.explanation: Average speed uses total distance: 120 ÷ 24 = 5.0 m/s, four times the size of the average velocity because the dog doubled back.

questions.question: Is velocity a scalar quantity or a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Velocity has both magnitude and direction.

questions.question: Explain the difference between speed and velocity.
acceptedAnswers: velocity is speed in a given direction
markScheme: 1 mark: speed is a scalar / has magnitude only
1 mark: velocity is a vector / is speed in a given direction
questions.explanation: The single difference is direction: velocity includes it, speed does not.

questions.question: Give the unit of velocity.
questions.explanation: Velocity has the same unit as speed.

questions.question:
A ball is thrown straight up at 12 m/s. The ball later falls back down past the same point at 12 m/s.
Compare the velocity of the ball at these two moments.
markScheme: 1 mark: same speed / magnitude of 12 m/s
1 mark: velocity is different because the direction is opposite (12 m/s up compared with 12 m/s down)
questions.explanation: The magnitudes are equal but the directions are opposite, so the velocities are different.

questions.question: Give two ways in which the velocity of a cyclist can change.
markScheme: 1 mark: change in speed (speeding up or slowing down)
questions.explanation: Velocity has magnitude and direction, so changing either changes the velocity.

questions.question:
The speedometer of a car shows a constant reading of 30 mph while the car goes round a bend.
Is the velocity of the car constant?
Explain your answer.
markScheme: 1 mark: the velocity is not constant / changes
1 mark: because the direction of motion changes (even though the speed is constant)
questions.explanation: A speedometer shows speed only. Going round a bend changes the direction, so the velocity changes.

questions.question: Explain, with an example, why an object can be accelerating even though its speed is constant.
markScheme: 1 mark: example of circular motion at constant speed (for example satellite in orbit, car on a roundabout, ball on a string)
1 mark: its direction is continuously changing, so its velocity changes
1 mark: acceleration is a change in velocity (per second), so the object is accelerating
questions.explanation: Velocity is a vector, so a change in direction alone is a change in velocity, and therefore an acceleration.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows the Moon in its orbit around the Earth.
The Moon moves in a nearly circular orbit at a nearly constant speed of about 1000 m/s.
Describe the direction of the velocity of the Moon at any instant.
acceptedAnswers: at right angles to the radius
markScheme: 1 mark: along the tangent to its orbit
1 mark: at right angles to the line joining it to the centre of the Earth (direction continually changing)
questions.explanation: In circular motion the velocity points along the tangent, perpendicular to the radius, and so it changes direction all the time.

questions.question:
Explain the difference between speed and velocity.
Use the examples of a car on a straight motorway and the same car on a roundabout.
markScheme: Speed is a scalar: it has magnitude only
Velocity is a vector: speed in a given direction
On a straight motorway at a constant speed, the direction does not change, so velocity is constant
If the car speeds up or slows down on the motorway, both speed and velocity change
On a roundabout at constant speed, the direction changes, so the velocity changes but the speed does not
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): clear definitions linked correctly to both examples
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): a correct definition or one correct example
questions.explanation: The motorway shows a case where speed and velocity behave alike; the roundabout shows that velocity can change while speed stays constant.

questions.question:
A student walks from home to a shop and back.
Table 1 shows information about the trip.
Compare her average speed and her average velocity for the whole trip.
Use calculations in your answer.
markScheme: Total time = 12 minutes = 720 s (includes time in the shop)
Velocity uses displacement (vector); speed uses distance (scalar)
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): correct calculations of both with a clear reason for the difference
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): one correct value or a correct statement about displacement
questions.explanation: Average speed = 800 ÷ 720 = 1.1 m/s, but the average velocity is zero because the displacement is zero.

questions.question:
A child sits on a playground roundabout that rotates at a constant rate.
Explain how the speed, velocity and direction of motion of the child change as the roundabout turns.
Explain why the child is accelerating and what this tells you about the force on the child.
markScheme: The child moves in a circle at a constant speed
At every instant the child's velocity is along the tangent to the circle
The direction of motion is continuously changing
Velocity is a vector, so a change in direction is a change in velocity
The magnitude of the velocity (the speed) stays the same
Acceleration is a change in velocity, so the child is accelerating even though the speed is constant
A changing velocity needs a resultant force (Newton's first law), which acts towards the centre of the circle, provided by the child gripping the roundabout
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): detailed, coherent explanation covering constant speed, changing direction, changing velocity, acceleration and the need for a resultant force
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): explains constant speed but changing velocity with some reference to acceleration or force
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple relevant statements, for example the child goes round in a circle at constant speed
questions.explanation: This is the Higher-tier idea that circular motion at constant speed involves a changing velocity, linked to acceleration and to the need for a resultant force.
